pages.text: The red colour is rust: iron oxide. Hematite ore and soil rich in little hematite spheres are your iron. Perchlorate soil is full of toxic salts: useful to chemists, bad for growing food.

Water hides as ice in the polar caps, under dust in dusty ice and in the ground of the high latitudes. The caps are topped with dry ice, frozen carbon dioxide, that turns straight into gas when it warms up.

Put perchlorate soil through a crusher to get perchlorate salt, the oxygen store of Mars. Crushed Martian or dusty ice gives plain ice that melts into water for the electrolyser. Look closely at the walls of the polar troughs: the caps are built of clean ice and thin dust bands, a record of old climates.
Mudstone, clay and gypsum only form in water. Find them in old river valleys and deltas: Mars was once wet.

Under the volcanic plains run the drained channels of old lava flows. Look for a round hole in the ground: a collapsed skylight. Inside, many blocks of rock overhead stop most of the radiation; every solid block above you halves the dose. A ready-made shelter for your first base.
